claims.statement: RAD-150 (TLB-150, TLB-150 benzoate) is a nonsteroidal androgen receptor ligand described by chemical vendors as the benzoate ester derivative of the SARM RAD140 (testolone), CAS 1208070-53-4, molecular formula C27H20ClN5O3, molecular weight approximately 497.9-498.0 g/mol, with an in-vitro androgen receptor binding IC50 of 130 nM reported by the supplier.

independent-review note (2026-08-29): MedChemExpress, an independent vendor/reference database from a different vendor family than Cayman/MedKoo/PubChem, was fetched live and corroborates the CAS number, AR-modulator classification, and IC50=130nM figure -- but all sourceRefs for this claim (including this one) remain vendor/structured-database listings ultimately restating the same supplier-originated figure; no independently published peer-reviewed structure-activity paper reporting this IC50 was located anywhere, so the supplier-only caveat stands and this claim remains without a genuinely independent literature confirmation

independent-review note (2026-08-29): live re-fetch of both cited FDA pages today confirms the quoted language is unchanged and confirms RAD-150/TLB-150/RAD140 are not named on the live Category 2 bulk-substances list (no SARM is named there at all); an independent systematic review (Journal of Xenobiotics/MDPI, Selig et al. 2023) separately corroborates that SARMs as a class are not FDA approved, but this claim's two sourceRefs remain both FDA-publisher-family -- no genuinely independent regulator, professional-society, or enforcement-action source naming RAD-150 specifically was found, so this is recorded as an open source-diversity gap, not resolved

claims.statement: As a class, SARMs (including nonsteroidal androgen receptor agonists structurally related to RAD-150's parent compound RAD140) have been associated in case reports with severe cholestatic jaundice resembling anabolic-steroid-induced liver injury in recreational users, with a typical latency of 2 to 3 months and presentation of fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, abdominal pain, pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice; the mechanism of SARM-associated liver injury is not established but is thought to involve excessive androgen receptor engagement. No case report specific to RAD-150/TLB-150 was located.

independent-review note (2026-08-29): an independent systematic review (Journal of Xenobiotics/MDPI, Selig et al. 2023), a different source family from the packet's sole original cited source (NCBI LiverTox), corroborates the cholestatic-jaundice pattern with 15 identified DILI case reports and a mean peak bilirubin of 28.5 mg/dL among recreational SARM users; none of these independent case reports name RAD-150/TLB-150 specifically, so this remains class-level extrapolation and stays fieldAuthorityRequired/human-review-gated, not resolved to a RAD-150-specific finding

claims.statement: Commercial vendor and bodybuilding-media pages market RAD-150 with specific claims of enhanced muscle growth, improved endurance/recovery, fat loss and physique enhancement, improved sexual function, and a longer half-life/greater potency and 'smoother' sustained effect versus RAD-140, along with numeric daily dosing suggestions (e.g., 5-10 mg/day or 10-20 mg/day for 8-12 week cycles); none of these efficacy, comparative-potency, or dosing claims are supported by any published human or controlled-animal study identified for RAD-150 specifically, and the compound is explicitly labeled by at least one chemical supplier as 'not for human or veterinary use.'

conflicts.summary: Vendor marketing pages (genemedics.com, muscleandbrawn.com) present specific human dosing regimens (5-20 mg/day) and efficacy/comparative-potency claims for RAD-150, while a research-chemical supplier of the same compound (Cayman Chemical) labels it 'not for human or veterinary use' and no compound-specific human or animal study was located to adjudicate either the dosing or the efficacy claims.

The only human safety signal available (SARM-class hepatotoxicity case reports and FDA's general SARM warning) is not RAD-150-specific; no independent source confirming or ruling out RAD-150-specific adverse events was found, so the safety claim rests on class-level extrapolation that must be flagged, not resolved.

Safety and dosing claims rely on SARM class-level sources (FDA general warning, LiverTox) rather than RAD-150-specific data; independent-source expansion should prioritize any compound-specific regulatory action or case report before this packet is published.

Remediation pass (2026-08-29): independent review confirmed rad150-regulatory-unapproved-sarm-class-001 and rad150-safety-classlevel-hepatotoxicity-001 (both fieldAuthorityRequired) remain supported only by SARM class-level sources -- no RAD-150-specific regulatory action, case report, or study was located anywhere independently (MedChemExpress vendor listing, Journal of Xenobiotics/MDPI systematic review, ClinicalTrials.gov, and general web/PubMed/PMC search were all checked). Per the Independent Review Rule this is an acceptable but still-unresolved gap; both claims stay human-review-gated and are NOT promoted as compound-specific.

Remediation pass (2026-08-29): the regulatory claim's sourceRefs are both FDA-publisher-family; live re-fetch today confirmed content unchanged and RAD-150/TLB-150 still absent from the Category 2 bulk-substances list. No independent regulator, professional-society, or enforcement-action source naming RAD-150/TLB-150 was found. This source-diversity gap is recorded as open, not closed.

Remediation pass (2026-08-29): confirmed the misinformation claim's vendor dosing text (5-20 mg/day) remains labeled strictly as marketing/dosing-page text, not a use recommendation, and must survive unchanged through any downstream editing or promotion step.

Remediation pass (2026-08-29): no PMID/DOI/UNII/DrugBank/ChEMBL identifier could be independently resolved for RAD-150 itself (PubChem, MedChemExpress, Cayman, and MedKoo listings checked); the identity claim remains anchored entirely to vendor/structured-database listings of the same general family.
